chapter_plans.title: The Terms of Reference
chapter_plans.one_line_summary: Iris Kane is appointed to the Kessler Line inquiry and immediately senses that the official scope is designed to conceal as much as it reveals.
chapter_plans.beat_summary: Iris Kane receives the letter of appointment to the national inquiry into the Kessler Line tunnel collapse. The terms of reference frame the cause as 'seismic microfracture compounded by dispatch error' and explicitly forbid examining procurement decisions above the site level. Reading the initial forensic report, she finds no physical core data supporting the seismic claim. She tries to contact former site inspector Dov Marek, whose signature is on the liner certification, but is told he has withdrawn from all professional contact.
must_happen: Iris Kane receives her formal appointment to the Kessler Line Inquiry.
The inquiry's terms of reference are outlined, framing the collapse as a seismic–dispatch failure and excluding procurement oversight.
Plant C008: Iris Kane notices an odd scope clause that explicitly insulates policy-level and procurement decisions from review.
Iris Kane studies the initial forensic report and finds no core-sample evidence of seismic microfracture in the archive.
Iris Kane is informed that Dov Marek is unavailable and has ceased professional correspondence.
must_not: Iris Kane does not visit the tunnel site or the Vantor offices in this chapter.
Theo Vance does not appear; the chapter is entirely internal to Iris Kane's process.
chapter_plans.opens_with: The body count arrived before the terms of reference. Iris Kane read the sixty-three names twice, then opened the letter.
chapter_plans.cliffhanger: Iris Kane hung up. Marek's assistant had said he wasn't taking calls. She hadn't said why. Iris wrote 'Marek — unavailable' in her notebook. She didn't like the way the ink sat on the page.
chapter_plans.signature_detail_hint: Iris Kane runs her thumbnail along the edge of the appointment letter, feeling for delamination. The paper holds. The text does not.
chapter_plans.emotional_beat: Methodical calm covering a deep professional unease as the gaps in the official report sharpen her focus.
chapter_plans.chapter_task: 1600-1900 words. Establish the scope of the inquiry, Iris Kane's voice, and the first political constraint on the investigation. Plant C008 through the terms of reference. Build intellectual unease, not action. No romance or romantic tension.
chapter_plans.carries_to_next: Iris Kane holds a suspicion that the inquiry's boundaries are not neutral. Dov Marek is established as a key figure who is conspicuously absent.

chapter_plans.title: The First Examination
chapter_plans.one_line_summary: Iris Kane's first physical inspection of the Kessler Line tunnel reveals a forged certification stamp and a direct contradiction to the official cause of collapse.
chapter_plans.beat_summary: Iris Kane visits the Kessler Line tunnel for the first time, accompanied by Theo Vance. She works her way to the segment Dov Marek certified and immediately spots an anomaly: the certification stamp is too fresh, the load rating code does not match adjacent segments, and the date falls on a weekend. Theo Vance offhandedly mentions he knew Marek professionally—a 'company man' who never made waves. Iris Kane marks the segment for a core sample, noting that the concrete shows no seismic shear whatsoever, directly contradicting the inquiry's stated cause.

chapter_plans.title: The Whistleblower's Document
chapter_plans.one_line_summary: Iris Kane contacts the source and receives the fast‑track approval document, which together with the forged certification reveals an internal conspiracy orchestrated from within the commission's secretariat.

They meet in a park; Watters gives her a single page: the Vantor fast‑track approval, signed by the office of the commission's secretariat—specifically, the signature line shows a deputy director code that Iris Kane recognizes as Theo Vance's predecessor, but the processing log indicates Theo Vance's terminal ID. Watters explains that he kept a copy because the original was 'adjusted' after the collapse. Iris Kane brings the document back to her apartment and lays it next to the forged certification report. The handwriting on both documents shares a characteristic slant in the annotations—the same person handled both the certification override and the fast‑track approval. She now has tangible evidence that the cover‑up was managed from inside the secretariat, and the probability that Theo Vance is involved is high. She photographs both documents and stores them securely.
